TITLE:
Report on Petition for De-Annexation for Sunny Side Addition, 4h Filing:
South % of Tracts 105and 106, Laramie County, WY.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kuker Group LLP, on behalf of Pendley, has submitted a de-annexation request to the City for a
information regarding thelocation of water and sewer within Monroe Avenue.The nearest sewer
hookup is actually located within 300’of the property to theNNW(Laramie and Monroe), not
directly infront of the residence.Once annexed, the continued use of the septic became illegal.
Per State statute, the Board of County Commissioners are required to prepare a report on the
impact of the de-annexation. This document will serve as that report.
BACKGROUND
The property is part of Sunnyside Addition, Fourth Filing, platted in 1945. Various replats have
occurred over the last 70 years.Much of what was Sunnyside Addition, fourth Filing hasbeen
annexed to the City as it has grown but many parts remain in the County.The general area of the
request has numerous County pockets within it.It would be difficult to develop this property
more intensely than what it currently is(a single family home)without it being an addition to the
City.
The attached petition provides the background, specific circumstances, and reasoning that have
led to the de-annexation request.
Pertinent Statutes
W.S.15-1-421 (a):
Any landowner within a city or townmay petition the governing body of the city
or town to havehisland or aportion of it de-annexed and the boundaries of the
city or town redrawn so their land is outside the city or town boundaries.The

county. The county commissioners shall, within sixty (60) days, prepare a report
on the impact of the de-annexation.The affected city or town may not take any
action on the petition for de-annexation until after the sixty (60) day period.The
commissioners may establish rules and regulations for the area tobe de-annexed
which are consistent with countyland use plans and zoning ordinances.
DISCUSSION
The impact on County services related to this de-annexation proposal is minimal, especially
given that it was recently annexed, and cannot be developed tomore intense uses without
connection to the City and the servicesit provides.
The following are comments received:
County Planning and Zoning:
The zoning on the property is currently MR-2 but will revert toMR after the de-annexation.The
property would be subject to County regulations and be processed throughthe County Planning
Department.Since thefees charged by the County are designed to reflect the services provided,
noimpactis anticipated.
The property would be subject to County building codes and fees.Since no development has
been proposed, and the development of more intensive uses severely constrained, theimpact of
future buildings would be minimal and would require a 201 Agreement should the septic fail,
and the single family residential be desired to continue.Building fees are designed to offset
expenditures related to providing service, so again, itis anticipated that there will be noimpact to
the County.
It should be noted that the applicants for the de-annexation of this parcel also own the annexed
parcel to the north that is adjacent the existing sewer system.
Board of Public Utilities:
Due to unanticipated economic development, the developer was unable to continue the
development of the infrastructure of Monroe Ave., therefore the water and sanitary sewermains
currently do not exist.
All construction, installation or modification allowed under the State of WY DE Q permit shall
be completed by November14,2019for this project.TheBOPU recommends that De
Annexation of Sunnyside Addition 4th Filing, S 1/2 of tracts 105 &106 be approved.

This office has not commented on or even seen a report completed by the Laramie County
Commissioners (as required by State Statute 15-1-421 (a) on the impact of this de-annexation.
(NOTE: That is the purpose for which a comment was extended to Environmental Health)
An engineering report showing that asmall wastewater systemwill not further impact elevated
nitrate levels in this area would be useful in protecting the public's health.
Cheyenne public seweris located adjacent to the owners property on Laramie St.Cheyenne
Public sewer is also located within 300' of the property to the NNW (Laramie and Monroe) and
to theESE(Charles and Cleveland)
Sunnyside Subdivision has a history of high nitratesin thewater table and small wastewater
systems contribute to elevated nitrate levels.
This property is still within the 201 Area and contiguous to the municipal boundary and will
require that an exception be granted by both the Cheyenne City Council and Laramie County
Commissioners prior to a permit being issued for a new small wastewater system.
CONCLUSION
Based on the comments received and the ability of County agencies to provide adequate service
to this property, therecent date of the annexation, and thefact that more intense development is
severely constrained until the property is hooked into City infrastructure, theimpact to the
County if this property is de-annexedfrom the City of Cheyenne is negligible.

3. At the time, Petitioners were told by government employees that an appeal would
be futile. Based upon expressed oral and written assurances from government employees,
including documentation on the official City map that shows “existing 8" water and 8" sewer
lines on Monroe Ave that can be tap for use”(Linda Gunter, Development Specialist, May 15,
2014, Clearance From The Board of Public Utilities), and that these water and sewer lines were

11.Petitioners filed a hardship request to do repairs, if and when necessary, to
the small wastewater system located onthe Property; this hardship request was denied on
September16,2014.
12. At the same time the hardship request was denied, Petitioners were
threatened by the Cheyenne-Laramie County Health Department to “abate" the small

according to City Ordinances.
13. Consequently, Petitioners then petitioned for an exception to the 201 Area
Facilities Management Plan for their small wastewater system until such time as the
sewer and water lines were laid on Monroe Avenue. The open ended waiver granted by
water lines has no time limits or restrictions. Therefore, Petitioners have no assurances
that the requisite sewer and water lines will be laid in a timely manner.
14. Petitioners’ request for an exception to the 201 Area Facilities
Management Plan was subsequently denied by the Cheyenne City Council on December
8,2014.
15.Petitioners have relied to their detriment on erroneous facts and misleading
Board, and the City Attorney were also misled; that is, they relied on the same misinformation

16.In order to place Petitioners in a position to repair the Property's small
sewer and water lines to be laid on Monroe Avenue and in order to have protection from
that the Property be de-annexed.
